title: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) for Intent→Configuration NetOps: Null Results on a Synthetic Verifier‑Checked Task Bank
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, archived paired experiment that tested whether a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop (Generate–Verify–Repair, GVR) reduces verifier-detected semantic invariant violations for intent→device-configuration translation. The confirmatory design used a public synthetic NetOps task bank (N = 240 paired tasks), gpt-5-mini as the generator, and a deterministic pybatfish-style validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). Execution used shared-initial-candidate semantics (one generated candidate per task reused across arms) and allowed at most one bounded repair attempt per task. All planned episodes completed (planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480) with model_calls_used = 240 (shared-generation). Every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms: n11 = 240, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0. The paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729). We document two preregistration/analysis issues evident in the archived artifacts: (1) the executed shared-generation semantics invalidated the preregistered power calculation that assumed independent per-condition generation, and (2) a prespecified comparison (GVR vs a schema-constrained baseline) was not executed and no recorded rationale appears in the archive. Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR provided no additional verifier-detectable benefit in this specific, artifact-grounded setting; the result does not generalize beyond the executed semantics, model, task bank, repair budget, or verifier.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→device-configuration translation with large language models (LLMs) promises operational efficiency but raises safety and correctness concerns: stochastic generators can emit syntactically plausible yet semantically incorrect commands that violate network invariants (reachability, workflow order, or security predicates). Prior work therefore proposes architectures that interpose deterministic validators and iterative repair (generate–verify–repair, GVR) to detect and correct mechanically checkable defects before commit.

We preregistered and executed a confirmatory paired experiment to test a focused operational question: under a frozen design that used a single generator/prompt pairing and shared-initial-candidate generation semantics, does inserting a deterministic verifier plus a bounded LLM-guided repair loop reduce verifier-detected semantic invariant violations relative to an unconstrained baseline? The preregistration, execution manifest, raw results, and analysis artifacts are archived and authoritative for all reported numbers. Key high-level facts from the archive: planned_episode_count = 480; completed_episode_count = 480; complete_pair_count = 240; model_calls_used = 240 (shared generation); n11 = 240; n10 = n01 = n00 = 0; exact McNemar p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). We state the final research question explicitly: Does bounded GVR (one repair attempt, deterministic verifier) reduce verifier-detected semantic violations relative to (A) unconstrained LLM generation and (B) schema-constrained decoding on a public synthetic NetOps task bank under the preregistered paired design?
sections.related_work:
Three bodies of prior work frame our study. (1) LLM failure and hallucination analyses document that stochastic models can fabricate or omit critical facts when generating code or structured artifacts, motivating deterministic verification gates in operational pipelines. (2) Generate–verify–repair and constrained-decoding techniques have improved mechanically checkable properties (syntax, compilation, or test passing) in prior code- and DSL-focused studies; these works suggest GVR reduces surface failures but leave open domain-level semantic guarantees for NetOps invariants. (3) NetOps literature emphasizes verifier-driven evaluation (reachability and policy invariants), intent‑based translation, and operator governance for high-stakes changes.

Closest prior artifacts used in positioning this run are included in the archived bibliography and were used to design the task bank and validator (see cited records). Compared with prior studies, our run is preregistered, paired, and artifact-archived: it enforces a prespecified primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline) and uses a frozen analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1). The run therefore evaluates operational value under strict inferential rules rather than reporting post-hoc comparative scores.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimands: The study was preregistered (study_id c1_gvr_semantic_eval_prereg_v1). The primary estimand is the paired difference in verifier-detected violation rates (guarded minus baseline) evaluated via the frozen analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 with Bonferroni adjustment across two prespecified primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B).

Design and execution semantics: Confirmatory sample N = 240 paired tasks drawn from a public synthetic NetOps task bank (12 clusters × 20 tasks). Requested generator: gpt-5-mini (model_configuration archived). Deterministic verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (pybatfish-style checks returning structured diagnostics including violation_count and explicit counterexample flows). Preregistered generation_semantics permitted independent per-condition generation, but the archived adapter run used shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial shared generation per task reused across arms). Maximum model calls budget = 480; actual model_calls_used = 240 because of shared-generation. Repair budget: at most one bounded repair attempt per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Missingness and exclusion rules were preregistered and are implemented by the analysis executor; execution manifest records zero infrastructure failures.

Scoring and primary test: Scoring rule = full_intent_constraint_validation implemented by deterministic_netops_validator_v5. The primary paired test is an exact McNemar two-sided test computed by the preregistered executor; absolute risk reductions and paired-bootstrap CIs (paired_bootstrap_percentile; 10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) are reported. The preregistration also specified sensitivity analyses treating failures conservatively as violations.

Evidence‑to‑claim mapping (concise). Each principal empirical claim below is mapped to an archived artifact path (no full SHA printed in the main body):
- "All planned episodes completed and model_calls_used = 240": execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/model_configuration.json and analysis/missingness_summary.csv.
- "Every generated candidate passed the verifier in both arms (n11 = 240)": analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv and execution/scoring/*.json.
- "No repairs applied (repair_applied = false for all episodes)": execution/scoring/*.json and execution/responses/*.txt.
- "Exact McNemar p = 1.00 and paired-bootstrap CI = [0.0,0.0]": analysis/results.json and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.
- "Prespecified comparison C vs B not executed": execution/execution_manifest.json and the preregistration file referenced in the execution manifest.
These mappings are intentionally compact; the full archived manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json plus the full hash manifest) holds the complete provenance records.

Nearest‑work comparison matrix (concise). We list representative nearby studies used for contextualization and state how our run differs: 
- Cadenas (GVR architecture / generate‑verify‑repair case study): shows GVR reduces syntactic/testable failures; our run is preregistered and paired with deterministic reconciliation rather than a single-case evaluation. 
- MeshAgent / intent‑based NetOps prototypes: demonstrates LLM-driven management prototypes; our run uses a frozen verifier and a synthetic task bank with formalized invariants for confirmatory inference. 
- NetConfEval / NetOps benchmarks: provides public tasks for configuration evaluation; we use a task bank that encodes workflow policies and a deterministic validator that returns explicit counterexamples. 
- Grammar/Schema‑constrained decoding studies: show syntax gains from constrained decoding; our preregistration included a prespecified comparison against a schema-constrained baseline that was not executed in the archived run. 
(Nearest-work entries are taken from the verified bibliography supplied in the evidence bundle; see cited_record_ids.)
sections.results:
Execution accounting (artifact-backed): The adapter run completed planned_episode_count = 480 and completed_episode_count = 480 with complete_pair_count = 240 and model_calls_used = 240 (shared_initial_candidate reuse). Deterministic reconciliation artifacts confirm provider-call accounting and that no infrastructure failures occurred.

Primary confirmatory outcomes: The preregistered analysis executor produced contingency counts n11 = 240, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv). Baseline_success_rate = 1.0; guarded_success_rate = 1.0; paired estimate (rate_GVR − rate_baseline) = 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00. Paired-bootstrap 95% CI (paired_bootstrap_percentile; 10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json and analysis/analysis_log.jsonl) archive the exact-test and bootstrap outputs.

Repair diagnostics: For every episode execution/scoring/*.json records repair_applied = false; the bounded repair loop never invoked because the shared initial candidate satisfied the verifier for all tasks. Representative per-task validation traces showing violation_count = 0 are archived under execution/scoring/.

Statistical interpretation: The observed contingency is degenerate (no discordant pairs), preventing estimation of a within-pair differential effect. The exact-test p = 1.00 and the zero-width bootstrap CI are deterministic consequences of the observed data and the preregistered analysis method. Crucially, the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation; the executed shared-generation semantics removed stochastic discordance potential and therefore invalidated the preregistered power assumptions for the performed run.
sections.discussion:
Conservative operational interpretation: Under the executed shared-generation semantics and the supplied synthetic task bank and verifier predicates, bounded GVR provided no verifier-detectable improvement because there were no verifier-detectable errors to correct—every shared initial candidate already satisfied the deterministic validator. Two artifact-supported mechanisms explain the outcome: (1) alignment between generator+prompt and the task/verifier distribution produced verifier-acceptable outputs deterministically; (2) shared-initial-candidate semantics removed per-arm stochastic variation and thus the within-pair disagreements GVR could have corrected.

Evaluation practice implications: Demonstrating GVR’s operational value requires evaluation semantics that restore discordance potential or introduce adversarial failures: (a) run with independent_condition_generation = true (one generation per arm) so GVR may act on stochastic differences; (b) inject adversarial or golden-reference tasks known to trigger verifier failures to validate oracle sensitivity; (c) expand generator families and repair budgets. The archived bundle already contains the task manifest, RNG seeds, adapter configuration, and the frozen analysis executor; toggling generation_semantics and rerunning under the same manifest would restore the preregistered inferential assumptions.

Threats to validity (artifact-grounded): Internal validity — preregistration/power mismatch: the preregistered power analysis assumed independent per-condition generation but the executed run used shared generation. Construct validity — verifier completeness: passing deterministic_netops_validator_v5 does not guarantee absence of other operational risks outside the encoded invariants. External validity — single model (gpt-5-mini), synthetic tasks, one-repair budget. Conclusion validity — zero discordant outcomes preclude evidence for GVR efficacy under the executed semantics. All of these threats are recorded in the archived limitations and reconciliation artifacts and are reported above.

Prespecified-but-unexecuted comparison: The preregistration listed two primary comparisons (C vs A and C vs B). The archived execution contains only one adapter-configured paired experiment (C vs A under shared generation); the schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) was not executed and no recorded rationale appears in the execution artifacts. We disclose this procedural omission as an unresolved limitation.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, artifact-archived paired experiment to test whether a bounded GVR intervention reduces deterministic verifier-detected semantic violations on a synthetic NetOps task bank. Under the executed shared-initial-candidate semantics and with gpt-5-mini as the generator, every generated candidate satisfied the deterministic verifier in both arms (n11 = 240), producing a degenerate null (paired estimate = 0.0; exact McNemar p = 1.00; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0], 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Conservatively interpreted, bounded GVR yielded no additional verifier-detectable benefit in this specific setting. Two preregistration/execution deviations (shared-generation semantics vs preregistered independent-generation power assumption; an unexecuted prespecified comparison) materially constrain inference. We publish the authoritative archived artifacts to enable deterministic reruns (e.g., enabling independent per-condition generation, adversarial/golden injections, multi-model runs, and expanded verifiers) that are needed to more robustly assess GVR’s operational value.

limitations: Synthetic task bank and verifier scope: N = 240 tasks were synthetic and evaluated against a pybatfish-style deterministic validator; results may not generalize to production topologies, vendor-specific syntax, or invariants not encoded in the verifier.

Shared-generation semantics: the executed run used generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one initial generation per task reused across arms), which reduced model-call cost but removed per-arm stochastic variation and thereby reduced sensitivity to detect GVR benefits that rely on independent per-condition generator variability; the preregistered power calculation assumed independent per-condition generation and therefore does not apply to the executed design.
Single-model evaluation: the experiment used one generator (gpt-5-mini); cross-model generality is not established.
Repair budget: only a single bounded repair iteration was permitted; different or larger repair budgets or iterative strategies might produce different outcomes.
Verifier completeness risk: passing the deterministic validator does not guarantee absence of all operational risks (unobserved invariants or properties outside the verifier model).

Prespecified comparison not executed: the preregistration included a prespecified schema-constrained-baseline comparison (C vs B) that was not executed in the archived run; the artifacts do not record a rationale, which is an unresolved procedural limitation.
